title: Descent of the normalized constant-module tensor square
statement: Let d, x, o and t be respectively GeometricData, ExactData d, OrdinaryIdentification d and FixedTensorData d [def-sfb-constant-module-geometric-comparison-data]. Choose scalar derived tensor comparisons cJ and cK [lem-sfb-constant-scalar-restriction-tensor]. For any natural isomorphism i between the localized pullbacks satisfying LeftLocalizationSquare d x o i [def-sfb-constant-module-derived-comparison-data], there is a DerivedTensorIdentification d x t for which TensorSquare holds with i and cJ.val,cK.val [def-sfb-derived-projection-comparison-squares]. In particular the ordinary ringed tensorator is exactly d.ringTensor.mu, the two derived tensorators have the specified K-flat representative equations, and the comparison square holds for all unbounded inputs.

theorem constant_module_tensor_square_descent (d : GeometricData J K A) (x : ExactData d)
    (o : OrdinaryIdentification d) (t : FixedTensorData d)
    (cJ : DerivedComparison.{u, v, w, w} J A)
    (cK : DerivedComparison.{u, v, w, w} K A)
    (i : d.pullR.mapDerivedCategory ⋙ onDerived K A ≅
      onDerived J A ⋙ d.pullA.mapDerivedCategory)
    (hi : LeftLocalizationSquare d x o i) :
    ∃ tensor : DerivedTensorIdentification d x t,
      TensorSquare d.pullR.mapDerivedCategory d.pullA.mapDerivedCategory
        (onDerived J A) (onDerived K A) tensor.val.1 tensor.val.2.2 cJ.val cK.val i
